name: Lighting presence detector plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a ceiling or wall sensor that switches lighting automatically according to occupancy.
description: Lighting presence detectors switch or dim luminaires according to occupancy, usually by passive infrared or microwave sensing. Plans show a small circle or square with a detection mark, often with the coverage radius drawn so designers can check the area is covered.

The plan should also show whether the detector operates in presence mode (automatic on and off) or absence mode (manual on, automatic off) and whether it includes a daylight sensor. These settings strongly affect energy performance and are often stated in a lighting control schedule.
This lighting sensor is distinct from an intruder alarm motion detector even when the sensing principle is the same. The two belong to different systems with different wiring and standards.
readingNotes: Check the coverage pattern against the room geometry.
Confirm whether the sensor controls a switching relay, a DALI group or a local load directly.
distinction: An intruder motion detector reports to an alarm panel; a lighting presence detector controls luminaires.
